slides.title: Status Epilepticus: The Clock Algorithm
slides.subtitle: 0 → 5 → 20 → 40 min: what to give, how much, and when to move on

slides.title: Definition (ILAE 2015)
slides.subtitle: Two time points that drive action
points: Convulsive SE: seizure **≥ 5 min**, or **≥ 2 seizures** without return to baseline
**t1 = 5 min**: treatment must start
**t2 = 30 min**: risk of long-term neuronal injury
Not waking **> 30 min** after convulsions stop: think **non-convulsive SE**, get EEG
Most seizures stop by 5 min: if not, they rarely stop on their own
slides.highlight: Treat at 5 minutes, not 30. The old definition delayed treatment.

slides.title: 0–5 min: Stabilise
slides.subtitle: ABC, glucose, access, history
points: Airway, **high-flow O2**, recovery position, suction; monitor SpO2, HR, BP
Check **bedside glucose**: hypoglycaemia → **10% dextrose 2 mL/kg IV**
IV/IO access; send glucose, **Na, Ca, Mg**, blood gas, CBC, AED levels, tox screen
Note **time of onset**: every next step is timed from it
Infant with refractory seizures: consider **pyridoxine 100 mg IV**
slides.highlight: Count pre-hospital benzodiazepines: maximum 2 doses in total.

slides.title: 5–20 min: Benzodiazepine
slides.subtitle: First line, may repeat once after 5 min
points: IV **lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg** (max **4 mg**)
or IV **diazepam 0.15–0.2 mg/kg** (max **10 mg**)
No IV: IM **midazolam 0.2 mg/kg** (max **10 mg**)
or buccal/intranasal **midazolam 0.2–0.3 mg/kg** (max **10 mg**)
or rectal **diazepam 0.2–0.5 mg/kg** (max **20 mg**)
slides.highlight: > 2 benzodiazepine doses = respiratory depression risk with little extra benefit.

slides.title: 20–40 min: Second-line ASM
slides.subtitle: Pick ONE (ESETT 2019: similar efficacy)
points: **Levetiracetam 60 mg/kg** IV (max **4500 mg**) over 10–15 min
**Fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg** (max **1500 mg PE**) or **phenytoin 20 mg/kg** at ≤ 1 mg/kg/min with ECG
**Valproate 40 mg/kg** IV (max **3000 mg**) over 10 min: avoid < 2 yr, liver or metabolic disease
**Phenobarbitone 20 mg/kg** IV if none available (and first choice in neonates)
Phenytoin: hypotension, arrhythmia, **purple glove**; never in dextrose
slides.highlight: ESETT: levetiracetam, fosphenytoin and valproate stopped ~half of benzo-resistant SE each.

slides.title: 40+ min: Refractory SE
slides.subtitle: PICU, intubate, continuous infusion
points: Secure airway, **intubate**, ventilate; inotropes ready
**Midazolam infusion**: 0.2 mg/kg bolus, then **0.05–2 mg/kg/h** titrated
Alternatives: thiopentone or pentobarbitone; ketamine in some units
**Continuous EEG**: aim seizure control / burst suppression for 24–48 h
Super-refractory (≥ 24 h on anaesthetics): look for autoimmune, metabolic causes
slides.highlight: Propofol infusion: caution in children (propofol infusion syndrome).

slides.title: High-Yield Pearls
slides.subtitle: Questions examiners love
points: Commonest cause in children: **febrile SE**, then CNS infection, AED non-adherence
First line in all ages beyond neonates: **benzodiazepine**
Neonatal seizures: **phenobarbitone** first
Hyponatraemia, hypocalcaemia, hypoglycaemia: **treat the cause**, not just the seizure
slides.highlight: Clock: 5 min benzo · repeat at 10 · second line by 20 · PICU by 40.

caption:
Status epilepticus: the clock algorithm every paediatric resident should know cold ⏱️

📖 Convulsive SE = seizure ≥ 5 min or ≥ 2 seizures without recovery (ILAE 2015: t1 5 min, t2 30 min)

🚑 0–5 min: ABC, O2, glucose (hypo → 10% dextrose 2 mL/kg), IV/IO, labs, note onset time
💉 5–20 min: lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg (max 4) · diazepam 0.15–0.2 mg/kg (max 10) · IM/buccal/IN midazolam · rectal diazepam. Repeat once; max 2 doses
🧪 20–40 min, pick one: levetiracetam 60 mg/kg (max 4500) · fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg · valproate 40 mg/kg (max 3000; avoid < 2 yr) · phenobarbitone 20 mg/kg
🏥 40+ min: PICU, intubate, midazolam infusion 0.05–2 mg/kg/h, continuous EEG

⚡ Neonates: phenobarbitone first · not waking > 30 min → think NCSE

Save 🔖 & share with your casualty team.
